_comment.1: Open-loop plant Bode of the x/tilt axis: command -> FSM -> camera -> CoM.
_comment.2: PARPORT-DAC version of conf_bode_x.json -- identical camera/CoM/sweep, with
_comment.3: anyloop:piplate_bridge swapped for anyloop:parport_dac (DAC81404 over the
_comment.4: PCIe parallel card). Everything downstream of the command is unchanged, so
_comment.5: this measures the SAME plant through a FASTER transport.
_comment.6: WHY THIS SWEEP EXISTS: the delay in steering_fsp.json / attenuation_fsp.json
_comment.7: was measured with the BRIDGEplate in the loop. The parport DAC replaces a
_comment.8: ~0.5-1.4 ms serial write with a ~12.8 us two-channel bit-bang, so the plant's
_comment.9: tau is expected to DROP by a meaningful number of frames. Run this (and the
_comment.10: y twin) BEFORE trusting steering_par_fsp.json's delay -- that file carries
_comment.11: the piplate-era value on purpose, see its _delay_warning.
_comment.12: K MUST BE RE-MEASURED -- it does NOT carry over from the piplate era.
_comment.13: Two independent reasons: (a) the fine channel is DIVIDED downstream, so a
_comment.14: given DAC volt no longer reaches the FSM as the same volt it used to, and
_comment.15: (b) scale here is 1.0 V/unit against the piplate config's 2.0, which halves
_comment.16: the volts per command unit on its own. The <=30 Hz |H| plateau this sweep
_comment.17: produces IS the new Kx. Expect it well below the old 0.915.
_comment.18: SOFTWARE injection: bode_plot replaces the x element (1; CoM is [y, x])
_comment.19: with a sine each iteration, and parport_dac writes offset + sine*scale to
_comment.20: DAC channel 1 (DACB) every cycle. Range 0-5 V, offset 2.5 V and scale
_comment.21: -1.0 V/unit, so amplitude 0.1 sweeps 2.4..2.6 V: 2.5 V +/- 100 mV.
_comment.22: No PID in the loop, so the command IS the sine = open loop. Phase is
_comment.23: from wall-clock time and includes the full transport delay.
_comment.24: TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage. ch0 = y/tip, ch1 = x/tilt.
_comment.25: y is parked at the 2.5 V bias (scale 0) while x is swept.
_comment.26: CHECK sample_rate against the achieved loop rate before believing tau: the
_comment.27: value below is inherited from the piplate era. The camera should still be
_comment.28: the bottleneck, but the DAC no longer adds to the period.

params._roi_note: ROI 64x64 at start_x 644 / start_y 318, centring full-sensor (676, 350) -- the beam position every ASI662MM config agreed on, carried over unverified. THE 662 AND THE 290 ARE DIFFERENT SENSORS ON A DIFFERENT MOUNT: re-probe with contrib/calibration-scripts/configurations/probe_frame.json and re-derive with contrib/calibration-scripts/tools/find_roi.py before the first real run. The beam also walks several px per hour, so re-derive again once |park| exceeds ~2 px.
params._roi_2026_08_07: start 1084/414 MEASURED AT THE OPERATING ROI, not from a full-sensor probe. A 6000-frame 64x64 capture at start 1072/404 put the beam at in-frame (42.0, 43.1), i.e. full-sensor (446, 1115); centring that gives start_y = 446-31.5 = 414 (grid 2) and start_x = 1115-31.5 = 1084 (grid 4), landing the beam at (32.0, 31.5). NOTE THE TRAP: a full-sensor probe_frame.json capture taken minutes earlier read the beam at (436, 1105) -- 10 px off in BOTH axes from what the cropped ROI says. The cropped frame is the one that matters, since it is the frame the loop actually sees. Verify any find_roi.py output against a capture at the operating ROI before trusting it.
params._gain_2026_08_07:
gain 0 -> 50. MEASURED 2026-08-07 by 6000-frame 64x64 captures at gain 0/50/100/150/200, scoring peak-minus-background per frame against candidate min_amplitude gates. The source is chopped, so the figure of merit is the DIM phase, and the cost of buying it is saturation in the BRIGHT phase:
  gain   0: amp p5/p50 = 21/90,  sat_p99 3.88%, 5.1% of frames under a 21.4 gate (55 streaks, max 40 fr)
  gain  50: amp p5/p50 = 38/109, sat_p99 3.00%, 0.3% under 21.4 (5 streaks, max 8 fr)
  gain 100: amp p5/p50 = 67/220, sat_p99 11.94%, 0.0% under 21.4
  gain 150: amp p5/p50 = 135/252, sat_p99 13.18%
  gain 200: amp p5/p50 = 192/252, sat_p99 17.04%
50 is the knee: it clears the dim phase while holding saturation at the ~2.68% the 08-06 com_survey characterised the Gaussian fit at. Above 100 the core flat-tops, which a Gaussian model fits as LOW amplitude and LARGE sigma -- exactly the signature of the 18:03 failures this replaces. Exposure is NOT the lever here: 400 us sets fs 2310 Hz and therefore the delay in FRAMES.

pipeline._comment: frame -> UDP viewer, so you can watch the beam + tracking (same as steering_fsp)

pipeline._choice: fit_com CHOSEN 2026-08-06 on measured data, re-confirmed on the stable centred beam. Same 60 s capture: fit_com hf 0.271 px / 11.4% rejected, wfs_com hf 0.814 / 79.9%, thresholded center_of_mass hf 0.639 / 22.9%. hf is the frame-to-frame difference, i.e. what the loop must reject -- fit_com is 3x quieter than wfs_com. wfs_com's rejection is NOT a geometry error: re-run at 3x3 and 5x5 grids with 6/8/14 px cells it stayed 82-88%, and only reached 35.9% with every quality gate disabled. Cost p50 17.4 us / p99 27.0 us against a 433 us frame period. The 11.4% rejection is the 4.7 Hz source modulation, not the tracker -- see com_survey.json.
pipeline._provenance: MEASURED 2026-08-06 by contrib/calibration-scripts/tools/com_survey_run.sh over a 60 s / 138600-frame capture at 64x64, exp 400, gain 0, fs 2310 Hz, with the ROI auto-centred first (find_roi put it at 1088/406, beam landing at (28.39, 29.95) against a 31.5 centre -- the residual is the 4-px/2-px ASI ROI grid, not an error): beam sigma 6.55 px / FWHM 15.43, amplitude 213.9 over background 1.74, saturation 2.68%. window 55 = +/-4 sigma; sigma_min/max and min_amplitude are 0.3x/4x/0.1x of measured, which is how com_survey derives its own suggestions. RE-RUN contrib/calibration-scripts/tools/com_survey_run.sh AND RE-DERIVE after any refocus or source change -- these are beam properties. An EARLIER set (sigma 6.31, window 53) was taken while the beam was being moved by hand and is superseded.
pipeline._shutter: NOTE ON THE CHOPPED SOURCE: the center_of_mass this replaces used ref_cut to drop frames the rolling shutter cuts through the source's on-window. fit_com has no ref_cut. It handles those frames through robust (Tukey) reweighting and the min_amplitude gate instead, and the 20.8% rejection above ALREADY INCLUDES them -- that number was measured on these same chopped frames. Watch it if the chop duty changes.

params._budget: max_us 25 is ABOVE the measured p99 of 27.2 us only just -- expect the guard to bite on the slowest few percent of frames, truncating those fits to fewer LM iterations. The survey's numbers were taken at the 10 us DEFAULT, so 25 lets the fit converge FURTHER than what was benchmarked, not less. Set 0 to remove the cap entirely, at the cost of a variable measurement latency that a fixed-delay model downstream will read as a wobbling loop delay.
params._regate_2026_08_07: sigma_init/sigma_min/sigma_max/min_amplitude/window RE-DERIVED 2026-08-07 from a 6000-frame 64x64 capture at gain 50, start 1084/414. The 08-06 provenance below is SUPERSEDED: the beam is now WIDER (sigma_y 8.74, sigma_x 7.69 over the brightest quartile, against 6.55) and DIMMER before the gain bump. min_amplitude 21.39 was the direct cause of the 2026-08-07 18:03 failure -- it was set as 0.1x a 213.9 amplitude that the beam no longer reaches on the dim phase of the chop, so fits were rejected 300 in a row and the tracker re-acquired several times a second WITH THE MIRROR PARKED, before any sweep drive existed. 10 sits below the measured p5 of 38 at gain 50, so it now separates 'beam genuinely gone' from 'beam on the dim half of the chop', which is the distinction it exists to make. window 0 = whole frame: at sigma 8.2 a +/-4 sigma window is 66 px, larger than the 64 px frame, so a 55 px window would clip the beam's own tails. Costs ~35% more pixels than 55x55 against a 433 us frame period, hence max_us 60. RE-RUN contrib/calibration-scripts/tools/com_survey_run.sh to confirm these against the fit's own statistics.
params._reacquire: reacquire_after 300 frames = 130 ms at 2310 Hz, NOT the 10 that com_survey's benchmark harness uses. This is the difference between the two failure paths downstream. A rejected frame (fsp.c:2141) holds the actuator command and advances the delay and modal state without training the observer -- correct for a frame the beam was briefly too dim to fit. BEAM_LOST (fsp.c:1960) zeroes the output, calls fsp_reset_after_beam_loss (xhat, the ucmd delay ring, plant and drift states, all transient state) and ramps back over beam_recover_ramp 0.5 s. MEASURED 2026-08-06: the 4.70 Hz source modulation produces 6 dark stretches per second, median 3 frames but p90 49 and max 201 (87 ms). At reacquire_after 10 every stretch over 4.3 ms takes the catastrophic path -- about 9 full observer resets per second, each starting a 0.5 s recovery that the next reset interrupts, so the loop never converges and the log fills with 'fit failed'. 300 sits above the longest observed stretch, so modulation routes to the hold path and BEAM_LOST means the beam is actually gone. Cost: a genuine loss takes 130 ms to declare instead of 4.3 ms. RE-DERIVE THIS from the dark-stretch distribution if the source changes; on a CW source it can go back down.
params._converged_fit_2026_08_07:
max_iter 4 -> 12 and max_us 60 -> 0 (uncapped). THIS IS A MEASUREMENT-CHAIN FIX, NOT A TUNING PREFERENCE. A 4-iteration LM warm-started from the previous frame does not converge when the beam moves far between frames, so it UNDER-REPORTS fast motion: at 200 Hz / 0.3 V the converged fit recovers a 32% larger fundamental (0.0934 vs 0.0706 normalized) from the same drive. Measured 3-way at 0.3 V over 5 points, 10-200 Hz:
  iter 4,  max_us 60, fit_slope on : linearity median 15.0%, worst 93.4% @200 Hz, K 0.5297, tau 2.784 fr, 0.045 ms/frame
  iter 12, uncapped,  fit_slope OFF: linearity median  7.7%, worst 68.3% @200 Hz, K 0.4179, tau 2.716 fr, 0.138 ms/frame
  iter 12, uncapped,  fit_slope ON : linearity median  5.7%, worst 24.3% @200 Hz, K 0.5154, tau 3.126 fr, 0.152 ms/frame
fit_slope MUST STAY ON: disabling it biases K low by 19% and doubles the residual nonlinearity, because the rolling shutter genuinely shears a moving beam across the 64 rows and the model needs that freedom to absorb it.
WHY THIS MATTERS FOR DELAY, NOT JUST GAIN: fit_com runs between the frame arriving and the command being written, so ITS COMPUTE TIME IS INSIDE THE MEASURED tau. The 0.045 -> 0.152 ms cost change is +0.25 frames on its own, and accounts for most of the 2.784 -> 3.126 fr shift above. The plant did not move. CONSEQUENCE: the loop config must run the SAME fit_com settings as the sweep that produced its delay, or re-base the delay by the difference in fit_com's profiled mean cost. Read that cost off the profile.c line at the end of each run.
Cost check: 0.152 ms mean / 0.224 ms max against a 433 us frame period at fs 2310.

params._tuning: v2 (2026-07-17): 60 log points x 49 cycles, split into 7 integer-cycle segments per point. The segment scatter gives the per-point error bar + a coherence quality (1=clean; <0.9 flagged as a disturbance line or drift inside the window). Integer-cycle segment boundaries (on excitation-phase crossings) kill the partial-cycle DC/line leakage the old fixed-time cutoff left in. 49 cycles keeps the 5 Hz window ~10 s, resolving it from the 5.64 Hz line.
params._amplitude: scale is 1.0 V/unit and offset 0 V, so amplitude IS the drive in volts: 0.1 = +/-100 mV about the 0 V mid-range bias, i.e. the output sweeps -0.1 to .1 V. Keep scale at 1.0 in every config that shares this K -- amplitude only reads as volts because command units ARE volts.
params._amplitude_2026_08_07: 0.1 -> 0.3, sized from the MEASURED Kx of this rig rather than the July one. fsm_bodex_par3_amp0.1.dat (18:15, gain 50, ROI 1084/414) fits Kx = 0.5794 +/- 0.0328 units/V at 64x64 = 18.25 px/V, against 4.05 units/V at 32x32 = 62.8 px/V on 07-31: the plant is ~3.4x weaker in px/V than the piplate-era-successor numbers, so 0.1 V moves the beam only +/-1.8 px and the +/-5.7% error bar on K (July: +/-0.09%) and 11.6% |H| flatness are ambient jitter, not a plant feature. THE CEILING IS SET BY THE BEAM, NOT THE DAC: at the current sigma 8.2 px, keeping 3 sigma (24.6 px) inside the 64 px frame caps the excursion at 31.5-24.6 = 6.9 px = 0.378 V. 0.4 V sits exactly on that edge, and tail truncation at the sweep extremes would be SYNCHRONOUS WITH THE DRIVE -- a systematic the lock-in cannot average out, unlike random jitter. 0.3 V = +/-5.5 px keeps ~1.4 px of margin at 3x the SNR. Re-derive this ceiling if the beam sigma or the ROI changes; note 4 sigma does not fit in this frame at rest, so a bigger swing needs a bigger ROI (which moves fs, and with it the delay in FRAMES).
params._amplitude_final_2026_08_07: 0.3 -> 0.15. THE 0.3 V COMPRESSION IS NOT THE MIRROR -- that attribution was wrong and is retracted here. Direct evidence: the CoM waveform captured at 200 Hz / 0.3 V is a clean sinusoid, 3rd harmonic only 2.9% (soft fit) / 2.2% (converged fit) of the fundamental. Slew-rate limiting drives a sine toward a TRIANGLE, whose 3rd harmonic is 11.1%; losing tens of percent of amplitude that way is impossible at 2-3% distortion. Most of the apparent nonlinearity was fit_com under-converging (see _converged_fit_2026_08_07), and it fell from 15.0% to 5.7% median once the fit was allowed to converge. 0.15 V is chosen because the plateau-K ladder measured across four drives -- 0.5699 (0.05 V) / 0.5761 (0.1) / 0.5582 (0.15) / 0.5113 (0.3) -- is flat to 1.6% up to 0.15 and only breaks at 0.3. Trust bode_plot's own LINEARITY line on this run over any of that: if it reports under 10% median at 0.15/0.075, K is good.
params._amplitude2: half-amplitude (+/-50 mV, i.e. -.05 to .05 V) linearity/dead-zone check: if |H| moves between the two, the CoM has left its linear region or the FSM is in its dead-zone, and K is not trustworthy. bode_plot flags >10%. The converter is NOT a candidate cause -- the excursion is ~2600 codes at 76 uV/LSB, sitting at mid-range with 2.4 V of headroom either side.
params._avoid_freqs: nudge sweep points off the measured bench lines (a line inside the lock-in skirt biases the point coherently -- segments do not average it out). List from attenuation6/8 memory.
params.config: x/tilt open-loop plant through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, range 0-5 V on a +/-12 V supply), no coarse stage, ch0=y / ch1=x. Drive 2.5 V +/- 100 mV, i.e. 2.4..2.6 V (scale -1.0 V/unit, offset 2.5, amplitude 0.1). 32x32 exp250 gain100 bw100, beam-centred ROI via start_x/start_y, tracked 20x20 thr22. Purpose: derive BOTH Kx and tau for this transport from scratch. tau: expect SHORTER than the piplate-era 5.8 fr, since the ~0.5-1.4 ms serial write is now a ~6.4 us bit-bang. Kx: expect WELL BELOW the old 0.915 -- the fine channel is divided downstream and scale is halved (1.0 vs 2.0 V/unit), so the old value is not a prediction, only an upper bound. K uses <=30 Hz; tau uses the full 5-300 Hz phase slope, so the sweep must run to 300.
params._start_delay: hold injection at 0 (= the channel parked at 0 V) for 30 s before the sweep starts. There is no coarse stage to settle any more, but the hold is kept: it gives the FSM and the camera AGC a quiet, known starting point, and bode_plot measures its baseline during it.
params._output_file: distinct filename on purpose: do NOT overwrite the piplate-era fsm_bodex_722_full7.pdf -- the whole point is comparing the two transports.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC. TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage: ch0 = y/tip (DACA), ch1 = x/tilt (DACB). Here y is parked (scale 0) and x is driven.
pipeline._range: 0-5 (unipolar, DACRANGE code 0x0), biased at mid-range 2.5 V so the command has 2.5 V of headroom in BOTH directions without needing a bipolar range. 76 uV/LSB over the 5 V span -- 2x finer than +-5 would give, since the whole 16 bits now cover 5 V instead of 10. The 2.4..2.6 V sweep is ~2600 codes, plenty of resolution and nowhere near either rail.
pipeline._avss_note: AVSS MUST BE -12 V (NOT grounded) on this rig: the steering configs auto-range to +-10 so the mirror can be driven negative on an impact, and the supply is shared. That means this 0-5 sweep also runs with a negative AVSS, which is OUTSIDE the condition SLASEH2A 7.5 characterizes the unipolar figures at (TUE +-0.07 %FSR, offset, zero-code 0.15 %FSR are given at AVSS = 0 V; the -21.5 V <= AVSS < 0 rows are the bipolar ones). It is inside Recommended Operating Conditions (7.3: AVDD 4.5..41.5, AVSS -21.5..0, AVDD-AVSS 4.5..43) and the bipolar TUE at negative AVSS is tighter, so the part is likely fine -- but the bode measures the plant THROUGH this converter, so if absolute gain accuracy ever looks suspect, this is one thing that is not datasheet-guaranteed.
pipeline._footroom_note: The 1.25-1.5 V output headroom/footroom figure does NOT set a floor here: SLASEH2A 7.5 conditions it on -10 mA <= load <= 10 mA (1.25 V) or +-15 mA (1.5 V). Unloaded -- the EC table's own condition, and near enough true when driving an amplifier input -- zero code sits within the 0.15 %FSR zero-code error, about 7.5 mV of ground on a 5 V range. Only if the FSM driver actually pulls ~10 mA AND the output must reach 0 V under that load does a negative AVSS buy anything, and then it costs the characterized condition above.
pipeline._scale_sign: x keeps the NEGATIVE sign the piplate config used (was -2, now -1.0). That inversion is a property of the optical/mechanical path, not of the converter, so it carries over even though the magnitude does not. It is what made Kx come out sign-positive. If the push test now says otherwise, fix it HERE and re-run -- do not fix it by flipping the sign of K.

params._no_range_max: auto-ranging deliberately NOT enabled for a sweep. A mid-sweep range change would glitch the output for a frame and step the quantization, both of which land straight in the lock-in as a bogus data point. The sweep never leaves 2.4..2.6 V anyway, deep inside 0-5. Note the STEERING configs DO auto-range (range_max +-10) -- the bode measures the plant at a fixed 0-5 range and fixed 76 uV/LSB on purpose, so K and tau are not entangled with a range change.
params._verify: off in a swept/timed run: verify turns each write into 3 frames (write, read-command, NOP) plus a non-posted status read per bit. Use it in a bench smoke config, not here.
params._skip_unchanged: still worth having, but expect it to skip far LESS than on the BRIDGEplate: at 153 uV/LSB a swept sine changes the code almost every iteration, where 1 mV codes often repeated. Costs ~6.4 us/frame, against a ~264 us loop period.
params._sync_update: left off. Only ONE channel is driven in this sweep, so there is no inter-channel skew to remove and sync_update would just add a SOFT-LDAC frame per iteration.
